{{Short description|Greek physicist (born 1944)}}
'''Leonidas "Leo" K. Resvanis''' ({{langx|el|Λεωνίδας Ρεσβάνης}}; born 1944) is a Greek [[physicist]] known for his work with [[neutrino]]s. He was a Professor of Physics at the [[National and Kapodistrian University of Athens|University of Athens]] from 1976 until he retired and became Emeritus Professor in 2011.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.phys.uoa.gr/an8ropino-dynamiko/omotimoi-ka8hghtes-kai-afyp-melh-dep.html|title=ΕΚΠΑ: Τμήμα Φυσικής - Ομότιμοι Καθηγητές και Αφυπ. Μέλη ΔΕΠ|website=www.phys.uoa.gr|access-date=2020-04-18}}</ref> He served as the director of the [[Nestor Project]].<ref>[http://www.symmetrymagazine.org/cms/?pid=1000014 Extreme Neutrinos] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120604041850/http://www.symmetrymagazine.org/cms/?pid=1000014 |date=2012-06-04 }}, by Katie Yurkewicz, ''Symmetry'', October/November 2004</ref>

Resvanis was born in [[Athens]], Greece.

Resvanis is also the person who suggested to [[Burton Richter]] that [[J/ψ particle|Richter's new discovery]] be named the "psi" particle.<ref>[http://ed.fnal.gov/samplers/hsphys/folklore.html Physics Folklore] by Lynne Zielinski (at [[Fermilab]])</ref>

==Career==
Resvanis received  his B.Sc. in Physics from the [[University of Manchester]], United Kingdom in 1965. He continued his studies at [[Johns Hopkins University]], United States from where he received his [[PhD]] in [[High Energy Physics]] in 1971. His dissertation was entitled "Measurement of the strong interaction form factors in the semileptonic decays of the long lived neutral kaon".

Between 1971 and 1976 he worked in the United States, in the [[University of Pennsylvania]] as an assistant professor. In 1976 was elected a full Professor in the [[University of Athens]].
